modules.name: math-and-euler
modules.responsibility: Scalar helpers (clamp01, lerp, wrap, distance, DEG2RAD) and XYZ Euler rotation / local-to-world point transforms used by every geometric and colour computation.
modules.notes: math.ts sits outside the named scope dirs but is the leaf every scoped module imports; included for dependency clarity.

modules.name: kit-schema
modules.responsibility: Zod schema, versioned migration ladder (v1→v7) and derived accessors for the physical kit description: drums, hoops, outputs/segments, RGB order, node layout, and kit globals.
modules.notes: Largest file in scope. Mixes three concerns: schema declaration, migration functions (shiftOutputHoops, shiftDrumOriginToCentre, shiftDrumToHoops, splitOutputDataLines), and derived queries. outputSchema uses z.preprocess to normalise legacy shapes.

modules.name: pixel-model
modules.responsibility: Materialise a KitConfig into the authoritative flat pixel array — world/local positions, tangent/normal, hoop and zone labels, per-drum bounds and pixel ranges.
modules.notes: buildPixelModel is one ~130-line nested loop carrying flip, per-hoop reverse, kit mirror, 1-based labelling and effect-origin derivation simultaneously. It is the single seam every renderer and the DMX map reads.

modules.name: dmx-map
modules.responsibility: Walk kit outputs → segments with one monotonic channel cursor to produce the pixel→(universe, channel) patch used by Art-Net/sACN senders.
modules.notes: The v6→v7 migration's byte-parity claim is a contract between this walk and splitOutputDataLines in kit-schema.

modules.name: pixel-grid
modules.responsibility: Spatial hash over pixel world positions for radius queries and nearest-pixel lookups by 3D point.
modules.notes: Not re-exported from src/index.ts — check who actually consumes it.

modules.name: color
modules.responsibility: Colour-space conversion (HSV/RGB/hex, gamma byte quantisation) and the per-channel blend-mode table plus buffer-level composite primitive.
modules.notes: Pure leaf; the natural place for hot-path allocation review (returns Rgb objects per call).

modules.name: project-schema
modules.responsibility: Zod schema and inferred types for the authored show document — layers, clips, params, modulation, transport, sections, songs, setlists, input maps and output settings.
modules.notes: Broad declarative surface; embeds kitSchema + migrateKit so a project parse implicitly migrates its kit.

modules.name: integrity-checks
modules.responsibility: Referential and routing validation over a project/kit pair — drum-id references, pad-key parsing, authored-graph keys, and hoop coverage/fan-out/range checks over outputs.
modules.notes: Two guard families with different error models (throwing assert vs issue-list) living side by side; routing-integrity claims 'a routing that passes here never throws in buildDmxMap' — a contract worth checking for parity.

modules.name: chain-wiring
modules.responsibility: Classify whether a proposed Output→Hoop→Hoop chain edge is legal given existing edges, returning a typed rejection code for the patch-graph UI.
modules.notes: Dependency-free pure classifier; a good example of a well-placed seam.

modules.name: defaults
modules.responsibility: Construct the canonical DEFAULT_KIT and a valid starter Project, asserting integrity on the way out.
modules.notes: Mostly literal data; the pixel counts here are load-bearing for tests and for the real rig.

modules.name: canvas-types-and-ids
modules.responsibility: Declare the canvas scene document shape (elements, gradients, sampler configs, lenses) and the `canvas:<sceneId>` effect-id encoding that hosts scenes inside the effect registry.
modules.notes: The id encoding is the adapter seam that lets canvas scenes reuse the single EffectGenerator interface.

modules.name: canvas-field
modules.responsibility: Evaluate a scene's 2D field: per-element colour sampling at (u,v,t) with gradients, plus UV-space lens distortions and 4D hyper-projection applied before sampling.
modules.notes: Both are switch-over-variant dispatchers on discriminated unions (element kind, lens kind) — the canonical place for a repeated-switch lens.

modules.name: canvas-sampler
modules.responsibility: Map pixel ids to UV coordinates under several projection modes and precompute a per-pixel sampler table so scene evaluation is a table lookup on the render path.
modules.notes: UvMode (4 string modes) and SamplerConfig (richer union) are two overlapping vocabularies for the same idea.

modules.name: canvas-scene-host
modules.responsibility: Adapt a CanvasScene document into an EffectGenerator (state, param spec, per-frame render) and keep a mutable registry of scenes plus the built-in preset set.
modules.notes: Module-level mutable registry; presets.ts registers by import side effect and effects/registry.ts does a bare `import '../canvas/presets'` to trigger it.

modules.name: modifier-contract
modules.responsibility: Define the ModifierDef contract (paramSpec, createState, apply over a PixelRange) and hold the static registry plus the category grouping the UI palette renders from.
modules.notes: registry.ts is a hand-maintained import+map of 20 impls; getModifier/listModifiers are thin. types.ts importing voice/modulation is the one madge cycle that touches this scope.

modules.name: modifier-impls
modules.responsibility: Twenty pure framebuffer transforms (trail, echo, bloom, blur, mirror, slice, feedback, strobe, grain, sparkle, hue-shift, levels, posterize, slide, kaleidoscope, freeze, flicker, chromatic, pixelate, strip) each applied in place over a pixel range.
public_interface: one exported ModifierDef per file, consumed only through modifiers/registry
modules.notes: Uniform shape by construction; several (echo, trail, feedback, freeze) keep scratch buffers in state and are the likeliest home for allocation or aliasing bugs.

modules.name: modifier-chain-runner
modules.responsibility: Run a resolved modifier chain over a framebuffer range in order, lazily materialising per-link state and optionally sampling per-link param modulation before apply.
public_interface: applyModifierChain(chain, state, fb, range, model, timeMs, dt, modCtx?)
modules.notes: An 8-positional-parameter signature; deliberately never throws on the render path (unknown modifier id is silently skipped).

modules.name: engine-buffer
modules.responsibility: The flat RGB pixel buffer, the layer-stack composite (blend mode + opacity into a destination buffer), and the RenderContext / TransportState / Trigger shapes every effect and modifier receives.
modules.notes: The narrowest, most-depended-upon interface in core — nearly everything in scope imports Framebuffer or RenderContext.

modules.name: engine-control-and-modulation
modules.responsibility: Hold decaying live control values (per-drum velocity, OSC addresses, volume), advance beat/bar transport from dt, and resolve a clip's authored params into effective values via LFO/control-source/curve modulation.
modules.notes: lfoValue takes `shape: string` rather than a union — primitive-obsession candidate; a near-identical modulation stack exists in voice/.

modules.name: engine-orchestrator
modules.responsibility: The legacy top-level render loop: owns the project, rebuilds pixel model and DMX map, queues and drains timed input events into triggers, renders each layer's active clip, composites, and exposes the mutation API the server reducer calls.
public_interface: Engine (constructor(project), tick(dtMs), applyEvent(event), setProject/getProject, getModel, getDmxMap, getFrame, getStats, setParam, setLayerProps, setActiveClip, setTransport, setOutput, addLayer/removeLayer, addClip/removeClip, setKitTransform, …)
modules.notes: God-object shape: render loop + input routing + section/binding resolution + ~15 CRUD mutators on one class. Instantiated once, in apps/server/src/engine-host.ts:62; apps/server/src/main.ts also constructs a VoiceEngineHost behind a VOICE_MODE flag.

seams.why: Lets an entire scene-document subsystem be swapped in behind the single EffectGenerator interface without forking the compositor.
New framebuffer transforms plug in by adding one file and one registry line; nothing else in core changes.

Registration happens by import side effect (`import '../canvas/presets'` in effects/registry.ts), so behaviour depends on module load order and global mutable state rather than on an explicit wiring call.
Version-keyed steps compose cumulatively; a new schema shape is added by appending one step and bumping CURRENT_KIT_VERSION.
Pure edge-legality decision, dependency-free — routing policy can change here without touching graph UI or geometry.

Roughly fifteen ad-hoc setters (setParam, setLayerProps, addClip, setKitTransform, …) are the server reducer's only way in; there is no command/reducer seam, so a new mutation means editing the Engine class itself.

Flip, per-hoop reverse, kit mirror, zone classification and 1-based labelling are all inlined in one nested loop; altering any one of them requires editing that loop rather than supplying a transform.
The modifier contract reaches into the voice subsystem for Mapping/applyModulations, creating the one import cycle that touches this scope and coupling a supposedly generic layer to the voice engine.

Two parallel engines (engine.ts/compositor.ts/modulation.ts vs voice/engine.ts/compositor.ts/modulation.ts) are selected by a VOICE_MODE flag in the server, so there is no single seam where render semantics are defined.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/engine/ vs packages/core/src/voice/ (engine.ts, compositor.ts, modulation.ts each exist in both)
suspicions.hunch: Two full render stacks coexist behind apps/server VOICE_MODE; semantics changes likely have to be made twice, and one copy may already be stale.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/engine/engine.ts (legacy Engine) and its only construction site apps/server/src/engine-host.ts:62
suspicions.hunch: If VOICE_MODE is the shipping path, the 438-line legacy Engine plus engine/modulation.ts and engine/compositor.ts may be maintained-but-unreachable in production.
LFO shapes, curve application and source sampling look reimplemented rather than shared; drift between them would make the same authored modulation behave differently per mode.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/modifiers/types.ts:23 importing Mapping from ../voice/modulation, and modifiers/chain.ts importing applyModulations from the same
suspicions.hunch: The generic modifier layer depends on the voice engine, producing madge cycle #1 (modifiers/types → voice/modulation → voice/envelope → voice/easing → voice/types).
Parallel switch dispatch over the CanvasElement and Lens unions; adding a variant probably requires edits in several switches plus types.ts and presets.ts.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/engine/modulation.ts:8 lfoValue(shape: string, …) and canvas/sampler.ts UvMode as a bare string union alongside SamplerConfig
suspicions.hunch: Untyped shape strings and two overlapping projection vocabularies invite silent no-op fallthroughs on a typo.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/modifiers/chain.ts (unknown modifierId silently `continue`) and engine/engine.ts renderLayer (missing effect silently returns)
suspicions.hunch: Render-path failures are swallowed by design with no counter or diagnostic, so a bad id shows up only as an unexplained dark layer.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/geometry/kit-schema.ts migrateKit — steps exist for <2, <3, <4, <5, <7 but no v5→v6
suspicions.hunch: A gap in the version ladder suggests a v6 change with no migration, so a v5 file may reach the schema missing whatever v6 introduced.
A full spatial-hash module with four public query functions that may have no live caller outside its own tests.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/modifiers/chain.ts applyModifierChain — 8 positional parameters (chain, state, fb, range, model, timeMs, dt, modCtx)
suspicions.hunch: model/timeMs/dt are already bundled as ModifierContext one line later; the clump wants to be the parameter.
Schema declaration, five migration transforms, and derived query helpers share one file, so unrelated reasons to change all land here.
getModifier/listModifiers/listModifiersByCategory are thin wrappers over a static map; the category grouping may be the only real behaviour.

suspicions.where: packages/core/src/canvas/sampler.ts:13 importing Framebuffer from ../engine/framebuffer, and canvas/registry.ts ← effects/registry.ts side-effect import
suspicions.hunch: Canvas, engine and effects are mutually entangled; the load-order-dependent preset registration could break under tree-shaking or a different bundler entry.
Two validation styles over the same kit/project pair; a rule added to one may not be mirrored in the other (mutation-parity risk).

items.coverage_notes: Read in full or in substantial part: engine/engine.ts (input + tick + mutators), geometry/kit-schema.ts (migration ladder and derived helpers), geometry/pixel-model.ts (buildPixelModel), modifiers/chain.ts, plus src/index.ts. Everything else was mapped from export/import signatures via grep, file sizes, and doc comments rather than full reads — so responsibilities are accurate at the interface level but I did not verify implementation behaviour for: all 20 modifiers/impl files, canvas/elements.ts, canvas/lenses.ts, canvas/scene.ts, canvas/sampler.ts internals, geometry/dmx-map.ts channel walk, geometry/pixel-grid.ts, model/project-schema.ts field-by-field, model/routing-integrity.ts rules, model/defaults.ts data, and the colour maths. I read no test files, so LOC figures for modules exclude tests and my depth calls are based on interface-to-implementation ratio, not on test coverage. Cycle data came from the repo's own node_modules/.bin/madge (read-only run): 5 cycles confirmed, only #1 (modifiers/types.ts → voice/modulation.ts → voice/envelope.ts → voice/easing.ts → voice/types.ts) touches this scope; the other four are entirely inside packages/core/src/voice, which is out of scope and which I did not map. I did not verify purity (no Node/DOM imports) exhaustively — no such imports appeared in any import line I inspected, but I did not grep every file for it. The VOICE_MODE / legacy-Engine live-path question is stated as a suspicion, not a finding: I confirmed both construction sites exist but did not determine which runs in production.
